```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE)
```


```{r load-data}
library(readr)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(car)
library(lmtest)


cleaned_data <- read_csv("~/Downloads/cleaned_cchs.csv")

relevant_predictors <- c(
  "PAADVVOL", "PAA_15A", "LBFDGHPW", "GEN_05", "GEN_01",
  "GEN_10", "INCDGHH", "EDDVH3", "FSCDVHF2", "DHH_SEX"
)

model_data <- cleaned_data |>
  select(LSM_01, all_of(relevant_predictors)) |>
  drop_na()
```


Compare two baseline models:
 Reduced Model: Predicts self-reported life satisfaction (`LSM_01`) using main effects only.
 Full Model: Adds an interaction term between physical activity volume (`PAADVVOL`) and perceived mental health (`GEN_05`) to test whether the effect of physical activity depends on mental health status.

```{r initial-models}
# Fit Reduced Model 
model_reduced <- lm(
  LSM_01 ~ PAADVVOL + GEN_05 + PAA_15A + LBFDGHPW + GEN_01 + GEN_10 + 
    INCDGHH + EDDVH3 + FSCDVHF2 + DHH_SEX,
  data = model_data
)

# Fit Full Model 
model_full <- lm(
  LSM_01 ~ PAADVVOL * GEN_05 + PAA_15A + LBFDGHPW + GEN_01 + GEN_10 + 
    INCDGHH + EDDVH3 + FSCDVHF2 + DHH_SEX,
  data = model_data
)

# Partial F Test comparing the interaction term
anova(model_reduced, model_full)
```

The partial F test produces a high p-value (close to 1), indicating that the interaction term does not significantly improve model fit. 


```{r initial-diagnostics}
vif(model_full, type = "predictor")

par(mfrow = c(2, 2))
plot(model_full, main = "Full Model Diagnostics")
par(mfrow = c(1, 1))
```
 Multicollinearity: Adjusted GVIF values are all below 2, indicating no multicollinearity issues.



Dropping (`PAADVVOL:GEN_05`)

```{r step-0}
model_no_interaction <- lm(
  LSM_01 ~ PAADVVOL + GEN_05 + PAA_15A + LBFDGHPW + GEN_01 + GEN_10 + 
    INCDGHH + EDDVH3 + FSCDVHF2 + DHH_SEX,
  data = model_data
)

drop1(model_no_interaction, test = "F")
```
`EDDVH3` has the highest p-value ($p = 0.4933$) and is removed next.

Remove `EDDVH3`

```{r step-1}
model_step1 <- lm(
  LSM_01 ~ PAADVVOL + GEN_05 + PAA_15A + LBFDGHPW + GEN_01 + GEN_10 + 
    INCDGHH + FSCDVHF2 + DHH_SEX,
  data = model_data
)

drop1(model_step1, test = "F")
```
 `INCDGHH` has the highest p-value ($p = 0.4353$) and is removed next.

Remove `INCDGHH`

```{r step-2}
model_step2 <- lm(
  LSM_01 ~ PAADVVOL + GEN_05 + PAA_15A + LBFDGHPW + GEN_01 + GEN_10 + 
    FSCDVHF2 + DHH_SEX,
  data = model_data
)

drop1(model_step2, test = "F")
```
 `LBFDGHPW` has the highest p-value ($p = 0.3285$) and is removed next.

Remove `LBFDGHPW`

```{r step-3}
model_step3 <- lm(
  LSM_01 ~ PAADVVOL + GEN_05 + PAA_15A + GEN_01 + GEN_10 + 
    FSCDVHF2 + DHH_SEX,
  data = model_data
)

drop1(model_step3, test = "F")
```
 `FSCDVHF2` has the highest p-value ($p = 0.2045$) and is removed next.

 Remove `FSCDVHF2`

```{r step-4}
model_step4 <- lm(
  LSM_01 ~ PAADVVOL + GEN_05 + PAA_15A + GEN_01 + GEN_10 + DHH_SEX,
  data = model_data
)

drop1(model_step4, test = "F")
```
`DHH_SEX` has the highest p-value ($p = 0.1235$) and is removed next.

 Remove `DHH_SEX`

```{r step-5}
model_step5 <- lm(
  LSM_01 ~ PAADVVOL + GEN_05 + PAA_15A + GEN_01 + GEN_10,
  data = model_data
)

drop1(model_step5, test = "F")
```
`PAA_15A` has the highest p-value ($p = 0.1052$) and is removed next.

 Remove `PAA_15A`

```{r step-6}
model_step6 <- lm(
  LSM_01 ~ PAADVVOL + GEN_05 + GEN_01 + GEN_10,
  data = model_data
)

drop1(model_step6, test = "F")
```
 All remaining predictors (`PAADVVOL`, `GEN_05`, `GEN_01`, and `GEN_10`) have $p < 0.05$. 


Resulting Model

```{r final-model}
final_model <- lm(
  LSM_01 ~ PAADVVOL + GEN_05 + GEN_01 + GEN_10,
  data = model_data
)

# 1. Multicollinearity (VIF)
vif(final_model)

# 2. Residual Diagnostic Plots
par(mfrow = c(2, 2))
plot(final_model, main = "Final Model Diagnostics")
par(mfrow = c(1, 1))

# 3. Coefficient Summary
coeftest(final_model, vcov = hccm(final_model, type = "hc3"))
```
